newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajik rebels breach border, peace talks to resume.
newsitem.headline: Tajik rebels breach border, peace talks to resume.

text.p: A group of Tajik opposition guerrillas has broken through Tajikistan's southern border from Afghanistan, a Russian border guards' spokesman said on Saturday.

The incident did not appear to be linked with fighting in Afghanistan, but Itar-Tass news agency said the guards had been put on alert because of tensions across the border, where Taleban Islamic fighters captured the capital Kabul on Friday.
In a separate report, Tass said Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov would probably meet opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri in Moscow in the first half of October for renewed peace talks.
The agency was quoting the U.N. Secretary General's envoy in Tajikistan, Gerd Merrem, who earlier held talks with Rakhmonov which he described as "exceptionally constructive and fruitful".
Merrem is trying to rescue a shaky United Nations-sponsored ceasefire which was reconfirmed at peace talks in July.
The ceasefire was first signed in September 1994 but both sides have continued to accuse each other of violations and fighting has broken out in regions east of the capital Dushanbe.

In the latest border incident, two Russian news agencies said that a group of more than 250 rebels had been trying to break through the border near the Tajik town of Kalaikhum for days. An unknown number succeeded at dusk on Friday, holding up three buses and a border guards' car.

RIA news agency quoted a source in the Tajik security ministry as saying that one of the Russian-led border guards was killed in the crossfire. But the border guards' spokesman could not confirm this.
The Tajik rebels are loyal to Islamic opposition leaders driven into exile in Afghanistan and Iran after losing a clan-based civil war which broke out soon after independence from the Soviet Union.

Lieutenant-General Pavel Tarasenko, the head of the Russian border guards force in Tajikistan, the poorest of the former Soviet republics, flew on Saturday morning to the border area, where fighting was reported to be continuing.
On the way he told Tass that the rebels may have been trying to reinforce guerrillas in the central region.
The border guards' spokesman said there had been about 30 attempts to break through since beginning of year, 20 of which resulted in armed clashes.

The latest breakthough attempt was two weeks ago. "This particular place is especially tough for the border guards," he said, adding that three had been killed and 13 wounded in clashes on border so far this year.
